card.name: Start of drug names beginning with B
card.fires_on: The lone letter b or B that begins a drug name split into pieces, such as buprenorphine, budesonide, bupropion or bexagliflozin. It appears in drug-interaction and warning text, often right after words like 'of', 'receiving' or 'increase in'.

modes.label: Buprenorphine start
modes.description: The opening b of buprenorphine in interaction statements.
modes.example: may result in an increase in<< b>>uprenorphine plasma concentrations.

modes.label: Budesonide or bupropion start
modes.description: The opening b of budesonide or bupropion when the name is split after the first letter.

modes.label: Capitalized brand or drug start
modes.description: A capital B starting a brand or drug name at the start of a sentence or after a colon.
modes.example: 5.1 Ocular Toxicity<< B>>LENREP causes ocular toxicity, defined

card.writes: It seems to help the model continue with the rest of a drug name beginning with b, such as 'upr' or 'ud', rather than ordinary words.
card.plain: It fires on the first letter b when a drug name like buprenorphine or budesonide is broken up, so the model can finish the name.
